description.value: River Safari offers jet boat and catamaran wildlife tours through BC's inland temperate rainforest in the Grizzly Bear Valley, located just off Yellowhead Highway 5 midway between Jasper and Kamloops. The onsite Forest Table restaurant — a floating-dock dining room with live-edge wood furniture and river views — has been independently voted the #3 Most Unique Dining Experience in Canada. Together with an onsite lodge and gift shop, this is one of the most distinctive full-experience stops along the entire Yellowhead corridor.

address.value: 6080 Mud Lake Forest Service Rd, Blue River, BC V0E 1J0

enrichment_extras.reasoning: Website content was fully available and served as primary evidence. The business is primarily a jet boat and catamaran safari/ecotourism operation with a notable onsite restaurant (The Forest Table, voted #3 Most Unique Dining Experience in Canada by TheTravel.com) and an onsite lodge; the OSM 'cafe' tag significantly understates the scope of the operation. Address (6080 Mud Lake Forest Service Rd, Blue River, BC V0E 1J0), phone (+1 250 673 2309), and email are all confirmed from the website footer and contact page, while no bike-specific amenities (racks, pump, charging, Wi-Fi) are mentioned anywhere on the site; however, the FAQ explicitly confirms washrooms are available onsite.
concerns: OSM name is 'River Safari' but the website domain (blueriversafari.com) and some page headings use 'Blue River Safari'; the website footer and contact page consistently say 'River Safari', so the OSM name is retained but the discrepancy is flagged.
OSM tags this as amenity=cafe, but the business is primarily a safari/ecotourism tour operator — the restaurant is prominent but secondary to the tour product.
The site is accessed via a 1 km gravel forest service road off Yellowhead Highway 5, which may be a factor for heavily laden touring cyclists.
OSM record has no address, phone, or email populated — all contact details are sourced solely from the website and have not been cross-checked against OSM values.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: The Forest Table is a legitimate and nationally recognised restaurant along a major touring corridor (Yellowhead Highway 5), with confirmed washrooms and full food service; touring cyclists on this route would benefit from the listing, notwithstanding the 1 km gravel access road.
enrichment_extras.notes: FAQ notes free RV overnight parking ('We allow RVs to park and sleep for free in our spacious parking lot, no hookups provided') — may be relevant to cycle tourists, though not confirmed explicitly for bikes.

provenance.category_correction_reason: OSM tags this as amenity=cafe, but the business is primarily a safari/ecotourism tour operator; Food & Drink is a valid secondary category given the Forest Table restaurant's prominence and the fact that non-safari visitors can dine there, but the listing may also warrant a Tours & Attractions category.
